issue.title: Agent-hood publication requests in the research hood stall at attempts=0 and never drain, so the outbox WARN never clears
issue.description:
DISCOVERED BY: sase-oc.land while committing the epic's landing integration work. NOT caused by epic sase-oc (shell completion) — the requests predate the commit by 31-42 hours and are in the 'research' hood, which the epic never touched.

OBSERVED (2026-08-17, workspace sase_12, athena):
'sase doctor --json' check state.agent_publication_outbox reports WARN. Project gh_sase-org__sase holds 20 requests: 0 quarantined, 0 retired, 3 stalled. The three stalled entries are

  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cdx      age 41.6h  attempts=0  last_error=null
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cld      age 41.5h  attempts=0  last_error=null
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.final_3  age 31.3h  attempts=0  last_error=null

each with reasons ['stalled: age >= 1d 0h']. The other two projects (actstat, bob-cli) hold zero requests. state.agent_publication_digest is OK with 0 problems, so this is not digest drift.

THE DEFECT: attempts=0 with last_error=null means the drain path has never once attempted these requests. Because they are never attempted they can never fail, so they can never accumulate attempts, retire, or quarantine either — they are invisible to every existing remediation. 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' does not touch them (it clears quarantined requests, and these are not quarantined); 'sase agent sync --drop-retired' does not either (they are not retired). They simply age indefinitely and hold state.agent_publication_outbox at WARN for every agent that runs 'sase doctor' on this host.

Contrast with the working path: during the same session a real quarantine (19 requests, 'file digest mismatch') was reported by sase_git_commit and 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' cleared it completely — quarantined_request_count went 19 -> 0 and the digest check went to OK. So the quarantine machinery works; it is specifically the never-attempted requests that have no path out.

SCOPE: find why the full-sync drain skips these three requests (a hood-selection or publishability filter that silently excludes them is the likely shape, given attempts stays 0), then either make the drain attempt them — so they succeed, or fail into the existing retry/quarantine/retire lifecycle — or give them a deliberate terminal state. A request the drain refuses to attempt should not be able to sit at attempts=0 forever with no recorded reason.

REPRODUCTION: sase doctor --json, then read checks[] entry state.agent_publication_outbox -> data.problems. Note the check identity lives on the 'id' field; 'name' is absent, so a probe matching on 'name' silently finds nothing.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-fi — closed task 'Prompt-archive publication has no durable retry path'. Its description states that agent-hood publication already HAS a durable retry via the agent-publication outbox, which is exactly the mechanism failing here: the outbox holds these requests but never attempts them. Its fix is working — this session's commit printed 'prompt archive publication was deferred and will retry with agent publication', the retry-with-agent-publication path sase-fi added.

RELATED: sase-hw — closed task 'sase commit quarantined-publication warning recommends a retry that can never clear v2 import identity collisions'. Distinct root cause: in this session the recommended 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' DID clear all 19 quarantined requests, so the warning's advice was correct here. The stalled attempts=0 requests are a separate class that no advice covers.
